scope: Synthetic in-memory code probes. No live Discord, PostgreSQL, credentials, or real-user data.

tracking.scope: synthetic, in-memory tracker behavior only; no production users, database, Discord, or network
tracking.retention_measurement: No real retention, activation, churn, or reminder-open metrics are available from these probes.

probes.risk_hypothesis: A seven-day streak becomes zero after one missed deadline; some returning members may find the reset discouraging. Best streak and solve history remain intact.

A member aiming for four days per week sees 4/7 participation without a configurable four-day goal or goal-completion signal. This may underserve non-daily practice schedules; no retention effect has been measured.

observed.second_same_day_attempt: Already counted that problem for this challenge day.

probes.risk_hypothesis: A legitimate same-day review attempt receives no additional counted activity and is not stored in history. This is the specified duplicate-count policy, but can frustrate users expecting a practice-attempt diary.

observed.direct_change_error: Leave and rejoin to change timezone; history and lifetime totals are preserved.

probes.risk_hypothesis: Travel or correcting a timezone requires leaving/rejoining and reduces the current seven-day streak to one, although all history and best streak survive. This follows existing rules and is a concrete source of avoidable friction if timezone changes become common.

The grid correctly distinguishes six unavailable days, but the headline still reads 1/7 participation with a partial-history flag. Users may interpret unavailable history as six misses unless the UI makes the flag prominent. This is a denominator/coverage mismatch, not demonstrated data loss.

Paused members correctly receive no reminder and their open leave day is excused in the report. Weekly progress still includes that excused day in its denominator (1/2), which can appear inconsistent with being excused.

probes.response:

Use `/quest`, then `/submit` with your actual attempt link.

probes.finding: Join confirms timezone/deadline and opt-out, then directs the member to quest and submit; the quest is available through a button but the join response itself has no problem link.

cases.error: Paste the actual submission link ending /submissions/<id>/, not just a problem link.
For a /submissions/detail/ link, also supply the problem_url field.

probes.finding: Problem-only URLs are rejected. A global attempt URL requires a second problem_url field; a problem-scoped attempt works in one command. This is intentional validation, not a data-loss bug.

Reminders are one channel message per pending member, not grouped. 100 pending members produce 200 messages across the two default slots. Transport is mocked, so this measures message count, not real rate-limit latency.

Personal opt-out works immediately and submitted members are excluded. Current control is a typed boolean slash command; no per-user quiet hours, snooze, or reminder-action button exists in the dashboard.

storage.scope: Synthetic in-memory fakes only; no .env, sockets, Discord, or PostgreSQL connection.
storage.timing_limit: Includes fake whole-table deepcopy/rollback overhead; not a production latency estimate.

failure_flow.failed_db_commit_response: Couldn't load or save that. Check the database connection and try again.

retention_observability.available_post_v3_signal: Persisted solve received_at/date, member enrollment periods, daily buckets, timezone/deadline snapshots.
retention_observability.missing_signal: No command-view/session/visit events, reminder impressions/clicks, exposure experiments, or precise original acquisition timestamp.
retention_observability.legacy_limit: v2 has lifetime totals plus at most 30 daily buckets; previous joins may have been overwritten; missing days are unknown.
retention_observability.cohort_caveats: Use first observed post-v3 activation cohort; exclude unknown coverage and right-censored users; leavers remain in original cohort denominator.
retention_observability.interpretation: A D7/D28 solve-active metric is not user-return retention and cannot be claimed from synthetic measurements.
